41-078.r: PESA rules → Gram Sabha meeting in Scheduled Areas is chaired by a Scheduled Tribe member chosen by consensus for one year; failing consensus, the oldest ST woman present.

41-079.r: 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 → foundation of strong, vibrant Panchayati Raj Institutions; the 74th Amendment Act deals with Municipalities.

41-080.r: 73rd Amendment (implemented 24 April 1993) → aims at a local self-governance system under Panchayati Raj.

41-081.r: 'Grass-root democracy' → Panchayati Raj (decentralisation of power); Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj in Rajasthan on 2 October 1959.

41-082.r: Panchayati Raj → local self-governance, three-tier governance with bio-relations, and 'Democratic Decentralisation' (Balwant Rai Mehta's term); not hierarchy construction.

41-083.r: Basic aim of Panchayati Raj → people's participation in development + democratic decentralisation; began 2 October 1959, Nagaur (Rajasthan); constitutional status by 73rd Amendment, 1992.

41-086.r: Local government attributes → statutory status, local community participation, power to tax; NOT central control (its aim is decentralisation).

41-087.r: Panchayati Raj's main aim → democratic decentralisation of power to villagers, so they make and carry out policies for their own needs.

41-088.r: Panchayati Raj → three tiers (Gram Panchayat-village, Panchayat Samiti-block, Zila Parishad-district); aims at economic development and social justice; MPs sit in Zila Parishad.

41-089.r: Wrong: '73rd Amendment came into effect on 15 August 1993' — correct date is 24 April 1993. Art 243-G (Panchayat powers) adds to its importance.

41-091.r: Panchayati Raj needs full cooperation of the local public; its goals fail without their support and participation.

41-092.r: Panchayati Raj represents decentralisation of democratic power, community development and people's participation — all of these.

41-093.r: Post-73rd Amendment (in force 24 April 1993) decentralisation → decision-making powers, the system as a whole, administrative powers; not judicial powers.

41-094.r: Decentralisation → autonomy, people's participation, empowering local communities; instilling non-confidence is NOT its feature. It extends delegation to the lowest level.

41-095.r: 73rd Amendment rejuvenated rural local bodies and reduced political interference in rural matters (A and R true, R explains A).

41-096.r: State Government has no authority over local bodies on citizens' complaints; it does control them in economic matters, law-making and service matters.

41-098.r: Name 'Panchayati Raj' for rural local governments → suggested by Mahatma Gandhi; he wanted each village a self-sufficient 'little republic'.

41-099.r: Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (set up by NDC, 1957) → reviewed CDP (1952) and NES (1953); recommended three-tier Panchayati Raj; Rajasthan first to adopt it.
hi: Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (बलवंत राय मेहता समिति)

41-105.r: Balwant Rai G Mehta Committee (appointed January 1957, report November 1957) → three-tier Panchayati Raj, 'Democratic decentralisation'; reviewed CDP (1952), NES (1953).

41-106.r: Balwant Rai Mehta (1957) → three-tier; Ashok Mehta (1977, report 1978) → two-tier; G.V.K. Rao (1985) → better representative character; L.M. Singhvi → local self-government system.
41-106.h: Balwant 3 tiers, Ashok 2 tiers: the later Mehta cut one tier.

41-108.r: Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) → democratic decentralisation through three-tier Panchayati Raj at village, block and district levels.

41-109.r: Balwant Rai Mehta tiers (report November 1957) → Village Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti (block), Zila Panchayat; Nyaya Panchayat is not a tier.
41-109.t: Nyaya Panchayat as a separate body came from the Ashok Mehta Committee (1977-78), not Balwant Rai Mehta.

41-110.r: Panchayati Raj first started in Rajasthan (Nagaur, 2 October 1959, by Nehru), then in Andhra Pradesh (second State).
41-110.h: R before A: Rajasthan first, Andhra second; Nagaur opened on Gandhi Jayanti.

41-121.r: Not a PRI committee: P.V.N. Rao. PRI committees: Balwant Rai Mehta 1957 → Ashok Mehta 1977 → C.H. Hanumantha Rao 1983 → G.V.K. Rao 1985 → L.M. Singhvi 1986.
41-121.h: Order B-A-H-G-S: 'Big Ashok Has Good Sense'.

41-126.r: V.K.R.V. Rao Committee is NOT a Panchayati Raj committee — V.K.R.V. Rao was an economist (UN Commission for Economic Development, National Income Committee).
41-126.t: Don't confuse V.K.R.V. Rao (economist) with G.V.K. Rao (Panchayati Raj committee).

41-127.r: Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) → Electoral Reforms, not Panchayati Raj; L.M. Singhvi, Sadiq Ali, Ashok Mehta committees relate to Panchayati Raj.

41-128.r: Ashok Mehta Committee (1977, report August 1978) → two-tier Panchayati Raj: Zila Parishad (district) and Mandal Panchayat (village group, 15000 to 20000 people).

41-130.r: Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) → replace three-tier with two-tier (not implemented); district, not block, as first point of decentralisation below the State.

41-131.r: Ashok Mehta Committee (report 1978) → recommended Nyaya Panchayats and a two-tier Panchayati Raj system.

41-133.r: L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986) → constitutional recognition and protection for local self-government; no political parties in Panchayat elections.
41-133.h: Singhvi = Samvidhan: both start with S — constitutional status.

41-135.r: Not matched: G.V.K. Rao Committee (1985) → administrative arrangements for rural development and poverty alleviation, not 'Planning at Block Level'. Dantwala → Rural Credit; Santhanam → PRI finances.

41-136.r: V.R. Rao → Rationalisation of Panchayat Statistics; S.D. Mishra → Working Group on Panchayats and Co-operatives; G.V.K. Rao → Administrative Arrangements for Rural Development and Poverty Alleviation.
41-136.c: Question prints 'G.K.V. Rao'; the book notes it should be G.V.K. Rao.

41-137.r: Part IX (Art 243-B) → three-tier Panchayats: village, intermediate, district; intermediate tier optional in States with population not over twenty lakh.

41-138.r: Three tiers of Panchayati Raj → Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti / Block Panchayat (block), Zila Parishad (district).

41-139.r: Gram Panchayat is formed under Panchayati Raj (not Khap, Caste or Jan Panchayats); wards elect Panchs directly; Sarpanch elected as per the State Act.

41-140.r: All three false: intermediate Panchayat optional below 20 lakh population (Art 243B); minimum age 21, not 30; Governor, not Chief Minister, sets up the Finance Commission.

41-141.r: 73rd Amendment → Gram, Kshetra and Zila Panchayat; Nagar Panchayat, Nagar Palika Parishad and Nagar Nigam come under the 74th Amendment Act, 1992.
41-141.t: Nagar Panchayat sounds rural but is an urban body — it falls under the 74th Amendment.

41-142.r: Territory of a Kshetra Panchayat (and all Panchayats) → fixed by the State Government; Art 243-C(2): seats filled by direct election from territorial constituencies.

41-143.r: Chhattisgarh Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, Section 127 → Governor, by notification, alters limits or headquarters of a Block (and Zila Panchayat).

41-144.r: Status 1999: Zila Parishad at sub-divisional level → Assam; Mandal Praja Parishad → Andhra Pradesh; Janajati Parishad → Meghalaya; no Gram Panchayats → Mizoram.

41-145.r: No Panchayati Raj Institutions in Mizoram, Nagaland and Meghalaya (per the book); Assam, Kerala, Tripura have them.
41-145.h: 'M-N-M' trio without Panchayats: Mizoram, Nagaland, Meghalaya.

41-146.r: Art 243M(2) → Part IX (Panchayats) does not apply to hill areas of Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Manipur where district councils exist — so 'more than one'.

41-147.r: Intermediate Panchayat names: Janpad Panchayat → Madhya Pradesh; Kshetra Panchayat → Uttar Pradesh; Taluka Parishad → Gujarat; Anchalik Parishad → West Bengal.

41-148.r: Jharkhand Panchayati Raj Act, 2001, Section 32 → Panchayat Samiti; its members are directly elected by the public.

41-149.r: Panchayat Samiti → intermediate (block) level; members directly elected by the people; called Kshetra Panchayat in Uttar Pradesh.

41-151.r: First community development programme (book answer) → National Extension Service; CDP (1952) had three phases: National Extension, Intensive Community Development Project, Post Intensive Development.

41-152.r: Panchayat Samiti → block-level (intermediate) body; Gram Panchayat at village and Zilla Panchayat at district (73rd Amendment Act, 1992).

41-153.r: Panchayat Samiti (block level) → an administrative authority; link between Gram Panchayats and Zila Panchayat; processes village plans for funding and implementation.

41-154.r: Panchayat Samiti → administrative authority (coordination and execution); Zila Parishad → supervisory and coordinating body.
41-154.t: Don't swap: 'supervisory and coordinating' describes Zila Parishad, not Panchayat Samiti.

41-155.r: U.P. Kshetra Panchayats and Zila Panchayat Act, 1961, Section 19 → Zila Panchayat Chairman elected by elected members from among themselves; Section 19-A → SC/ST/OBC reservation.

41-156.r: Chhattisgarh Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, Section 39(3) → if Zila Panchayat President is suspended, a special meeting within fifteen days; members elect a temporary President.

41-157.r: Madhya Pradesh Zila Panchayat standing committees → General Administration, Agriculture, Education, Communication and Works, Co-operation and Industries (five).

41-158.r: Not legal: a woman Sarpanch cannot send her husband to Gram or Janpad Panchayat meetings; ex-officio MLAs and MPs (Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha) may nominate representatives.

41-159.r: 73rd Amendment → Panchayat elections made mandatory, held by a State Election Commission (Art 243-K), to make them as fair as Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha polls.

41-160.r: False: 'no separate category of local governance'. The Constitution provides for local governance in Art 40, Part IX and Part IX-A.

41-161.r: State Election Commission [Arts 243-K(1), 243-ZA(1)] → prepares electoral rolls and conducts all elections to Panchayats and Municipalities.

41-162.r: Art 243ZA → State Election Commission (of Art 243K) controls electoral rolls and all elections to Municipalities.
41-162.t: 243K = Panchayat elections; 243ZA = Municipal elections — the same State Election Commission handles both.

41-163.r: All Panchayat elections → State Election Commission (Art 243K); Municipal elections also SEC (Art 243ZA); State Election Commissioner appointed by the Governor.

41-165.r: State Election Commissioner (Panchayat elections, Art 243K) → appointed by the Governor of the State.

41-167.r: Rajasthan State Election Commission → constituted July 1994 (not December); one-member body; its secretary is also the State's Chief Electoral Officer.

41-168.r: Rajasthan State Election Commission → set up July 1994 under Art 243K; single-member, headed by State Election Commissioner; holds PRI and municipal elections.

41-169.r: Madhya Pradesh State Election Commission → constituted 1 February 1994 (under Arts 243-K and 243-ZA).

41-170.r: State Election Commissioner → appointed by the Governor (Art 243K); question deleted because it said 'State Chief Election Commissioner'.
41-170.c: No answer: the Commission deleted the question for its wrong term 'State Chief Election Commissioner'.

41-171.r: Chhattisgarh Panchayat Nirvachan Niyam, 1995, Section 46 → candidate dies before polling: poll postponed only if one candidate is left; not postponed if more remain.

41-172.r: Chhattisgarh Panchayat polls → one District Election Officer; one or more Returning Officers, appointed by SEC (or DEO with its consent); Naib Tehsildar can be RO for Janpad/Gram Panchayat.

41-173.r: Panchayati Raj elections are held under the State Election Commission; Zila Parishad is not wholly directly elected (ex-officio MPs, MLAs, Samiti heads); contest age is not 18.

41-174.r: Art 243-F(1) → minimum age to be a Panchayat member: 21 years.
41-174.t: Voting age is 18, but contesting a Panchayat seat needs 21.

41-175.r: 73rd Amendment → minimum age to contest Panchayati Raj elections: 21 years.

41-176.r: Panchayat member minimum age → 21 (not 25); Panchayat reconstituted after early dissolution serves only the remainder of the term (Art 243E).

41-177.r: To contest a Municipal Council election, one's name must be in that municipality's electoral roll; party membership or college permission is not needed.

41-178.r: Art 243(I) → Governor constitutes a Finance Commission within one year of the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 and every fifth year after, to review Panchayat finances.

41-179.r: Panchayat finances → reviewed by a State Finance Commission constituted by the Governor under Art 243-I (Part IX); it recommends to the Governor.

41-181.r: Every five years, a Finance Commission (Art 243I, set up by the Governor) reviews Panchayat finances — a commission, not a committee.

41-182.r: State Finance Commission (Art 243I, set up by the Governor) → recommends how revenue is shared between the State Government and local governments.

41-183.r: Art 243(I) → State Finance Commission, to review finances of Panchayati Raj Institutions.
41-183.h: 243 I-J-K: I = Income (Finance Commission), J = Jaanch (audit), K = Kaun jeetega (elections).

41-184.r: State Finance Commission (Art 243I) → recommends to the Governor principles for taxes, duties, tolls and fees assigned to or taken by Panchayats.

41-186.r: A false, R true: Union Finance Commission (Art 280) does recommend measures to boost State funds for Panchayats and Municipalities; local government stays a State subject.

41-187.r: State Election Commission → constitutional body (73rd and 74th Amendments, 1992); it, not the Election Commission of India, conducts all local body elections.

41-188.r: Constitutional authorities: State Election Commission (Art 243K), State Finance Commission (243I), District Panchayat (243B); State/Chief Electoral Officer is not.

41-189.r: Part IX-A → Municipalities; added by the 74th Amendment Act, 1992; in force from 1st June 1993.

41-190.r: 74th Amendment Act, 1992 (in force 1 June 1993) → Part IX-A (Arts 243P-243ZG), new 12th Schedule with 18 items, women's seats in Municipalities; not limited to some States.

41-191.r: 74th Amendment, 1992 → constitutional status to Municipalities (urban local bodies): Part IX-A (Arts 243P-243ZG) and the 12th Schedule.
41-191.h: 73 = gaon (village), 74 = shahar (town): one number up, one step up to the town.

41-195.r: Municipality member: minimum age 21, not 25 (Art 243V); not less than one-third of directly elected municipal seats reserved for women (Art 243T(3)).

41-196.r: Art 243T(1) → reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in Municipalities (asked for Madhya Pradesh).

41-197.r: Rajasthan Mayor election security deposit → Rs. 30,000 for general candidates; Rs. 15,000 for women, SC, ST and Backward Class candidates.

41-198.r: Mayor's tenure → 5 years, as Municipal Corporation's term is 5 years (Art 243U); exceptions: Delhi and Bengaluru one year, Mumbai 2.5 years.

41-199.r: Census urban area: population at least 5000, at least 75% (not 60%) of working men in non-farm work, density at least 400 per sq km.
41-199.t: The trap is 60%; the Census rule is 75% of male workers in non-agricultural work.

41-200.r: Art 243Q → Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area; big cities get corporations because their administration is very complex (A and R true, R explains A).

41-201.r: Chhattisgarh Municipalities Act, 1961, Section 79(2) → Panchayat vs Cantonment Board disputes decided by the State Government with Central Government's concurrence.

41-202.r: Art 243P(d) → Municipal area = territorial area of a Municipality as notified by the Governor.

41-203.r: Rajasthan Municipal Act, 2009 → State Government may nominate up to 6 in a municipal board, 8 in a municipal council, 12 in a municipal corporation.
41-203.h: 6-8-12: nominations grow with size — board, council, corporation.

41-204.r: Art 243V → minimum age for Municipality membership is 21 years; a 21-year-old cannot be disqualified on the ground of age.

41-205.r: Chhattisgarh Municipalities Act, 1961, Section 34 → a voter on the municipal roll may contest: President at 25+, Councillor at 21+; cannot contest from two wards at once.

41-206.r: Municipal council term → 5 years from the date of its first meeting (not result day); after dissolution, election within six months.

41-207.r: Chhattisgarh Municipalities Act, 1961, Section 47 → President recalled by secret ballot of more than half of voters voting; proposal signed by 3/4 elected councillors.

41-208.r: Art 243S → ward committees (population three lakh or more); elected ward councillors are members; Chhattisgarh adds two nominated ward residents; chairman not nominated by Nagar Panchayat President.

41-209.r: Chhattisgarh: a Councillor who acts as legal practitioner for another person against the Municipal Council is removed from office by the Collector.

41-210.r: U.P. Municipality chairman → elected directly by voters on the area's electoral list, including electors of wards (statements 2 and 4).

41-211.r: Ghaziabad → Nagar Nigam (Municipal Corporation), not Nagarpalika Parishad; Kanpur Nagar Nigam; Lucknow Cantonment Board; Kakori Nagar Panchayat (Lucknow).

41-212.r: 73rd/74th Amendments created: State Election Commission (243-K, 243-ZA), State Finance Commission (243-I, 243-Y), District Planning Committee (243-ZD); not State Property Tax Valuation Board.

41-213.r: 73rd Amendment → State Election Commissions for Panchayat polls (243K) and State Finance Commissions (243-I); District Planning Committees come from the 74th (Art 243ZD).
41-213.t: District Planning Committee (243ZD) is in Part IX-A — 74th Amendment, not 73rd.

41-214.r: Rajasthan District Planning Committee → 20 elected and 5 ex-officio members (varies by State: Bihar 34 members, Chhattisgarh 20).

41-215.r: Art 243ZD → District Planning Committee: consolidates plans of Panchayats and Municipalities and prepares a draft development plan for the district.

41-216.r: Rajasthan: Zila Pramukh chairs the District Planning Committee (Section 121, Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act, 1994; DPC under Art 243ZD).

41-217.r: District Plan in U.P. covers Nagar Panchayat, Gram Panchayat and Kshetra (Block) Panchayat; Planning Commission's first district-planning guidelines came in 1969.
41-217.c: Explanation lists District Panchayat, not Nagar Panchayat (item I), though the answer counts I.
